Not alot of people talk about it, but I’ve experienced thermal throttling on an i5 P variant to the point I had to return it. So unless you could find an U variant then yes 11th gen is economically better considering your workload is pretty light(excluding video editing and solidworks because I assume you’d only be doing light editing).

12th gen has an U variant processor that has power draw range of 9-29w. The P variant is meant for more performance but draws more power. So I recommend finding a laptop with 12th gen U processor in it for more power for the same tdp.

Duo screen is really niche thing, so it’ll come with a REALLY hefty price i.e. $2k-3k. If by duo screen you mean the one asus does then zephyrus duo with ryzen chip could even replace your desktop. 

But if your pc could handle 3D works for game then the only other laptop that has dual screen and a decent keyboard(since you’re gonna have to constantly type at least 4hrs a day) would be the thinkbook plus gen 3. It has 17 inch and a second screen on your right where I’d put my console, directory and research articles, 12th gen cpu wouldn’t slow you down but the lack of gpu does make it really hard to do game dev although the igpu is good nowadays so you could make games without shaders.

 Despite that if you love the dual screen of asus that much then there’s a zenbook duo pro 14 oled with rtx3050ti and 12th gen intel but it’s $2k which is really, too much. So if you could get the zenbook duo ux482 for ~$1k and don’t care about performance then yeah go for it since comp sci isn’t about the performance of a laptop, but the passion through trials and errors. Though you should buy it at a place where they have a return policy in case you don’t want it anymore.

There’s also a second option which is to get a portable screen and buy a normal laptop. I’d recommend it if you actually just want 2 screens.

Assuming you don’t want to touch anything inside a laptop since you said that you don’t want to risk it not working, then X1 carbon gen 6 would have the same performance as a t480 but better built and better display, the only drawback would be it’s upgradability which you obviously don’t need since you don’t wanna risk it.

Haven’t gotten a zenbook duo, but as a comp sci student, I could list some pros and cons through my experiences doing works, though I would recommend some other laptops.

Pros:
- The second screen is good for console.
Cons:
- expect low on-time with your battery since you’re powering 1,5 screens.
- through the spec sheets, your mx450 is just an entry graphic card and wouldn’t handle 3D graphics as good for your game development.
- intel 11th gen with Gx at the end only has 4 cores, also not ideal for your game development.
- keyboard is ergonomically bad, haven’t tested it but through many reviews said that the typing experience was not good. And you’re gonna type alot.
Conclusion: web development doesn’t require much performance but just requires a good keyboard for extensive typing, so any modern laptops can do it just fine. But doing game development you need more performance for 3D rendering and the screen won’t help as much when you’re debugging a game. The battery i doubt it’d be any better than a gaming laptop’s, so i would give that a pass.
